phrases.explanation: They tell one another not to march in the heat. The excuse focuses on immediate discomfort, while the verse contrasts it with the far greater consequence of rejecting responsibility. The Prophet is told to remind them that Hell is hotter than the weather they fear. The comparison challenges short-term avoidance and urges reflection on lasting consequences. If they could comprehend, they would weigh temporary discomfort against the Hereafter. The verse treats insight as understanding the moral meaning of a choice, not merely recognizing the temperature.

phrases.translation: So let them laugh a little—they will weep much as a reward for what they have committed
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites’ brief laughter is contrasted with the grief that follows. The verse portrays worldly enjoyment as temporary when it is built on wrongdoing and defiance. They will weep much as a consequence of their deeds. The warning turns their current celebration into a reminder that choices have lasting outcomes beyond the present moment.

phrases.translation: If Allah returns you ˹O Prophet˺ to a group of them and they ask to go forth with you,
phrases.explanation: The verse imagines the hypocrites asking to join a later expedition. Their request comes after their earlier refusal, so the Prophet is instructed to consider the pattern rather than accept a sudden change of words.

phrases.translation: say, “You will not ever go forth or fight an enemy along with me. You preferred to stay behind the first time, so stay with those ˹helpless˺ who remain behind.”
phrases.explanation: They are told they will not join the Prophet in another campaign. The instruction reflects the consequence of their earlier choice to remain behind in defiance. Because they preferred staying behind, they are directed to remain with those who do not march. The verse links opportunity with responsibility and treats their prior refusal as meaningful.

phrases.translation: And do not ever offer ˹funeral˺ prayers for any of their dead,
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed not to offer funeral prayer for the hypocrites described here. The restriction concerns people who died in persistent disbelief and rebellion, not every person who struggled with faith.

phrases.translation: nor stand by their grave ˹at burial˺, for they have lost faith in Allah and His Messenger and died rebellious
phrases.explanation: He is also told not to stand at their graves for burial. The instruction marks a boundary in religious solidarity after their rejection and death in rebellion. The stated reason is that they lost faith in Allah and the Messenger and died rebellious. The verse grounds the instruction in their final condition as described in the passage.

phrases.translation: And let neither their wealth nor children impress you ˹O Prophet˺. Allah only intends to torment them through these things in this world, and ˹then˺ their souls will depart while they are disbelievers
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to be impressed by the hypocrites’ wealth or children. Their visible prosperity should not be mistaken for sincere faith or for Allah’s approval. In this context, their wealth and family become part of their trial. The verse does not say every blessing is punishment, but warns that these gifts cannot guarantee a good outcome. They will die as disbelievers despite their possessions. The warning focuses on the final state of faith, which matters more than temporary wealth or family status.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sûrah is revealed stating, “Believe in Allah and struggle along with His Messenger,” the rich among them would ask to be exempt, saying, “Leave us with those who remain behind.”
phrases.explanation: When a revelation calls believers to faith and struggle, the rich hypocrites ask to be excused. The response exposes how material comfort shapes their priorities when duty becomes demanding. They ask to stay with those who do not march. The request echoes earlier excuses and shows a repeated preference for safety and ease over the community’s call. The verse contrasts their wealth with their unwillingness to support the cause. Possessions do not prove loyalty when their owners refuse to act on the obligations of faith.

phrases.translation: They preferred to stay behind with the helpless, and their hearts have been sealed so they do not comprehend
phrases.explanation: They choose to stay with people who do not take part. The verse presents this as a preference, not as an inability, and connects it to their reluctance in the previous verse. Their hearts are sealed so they do not comprehend. The verse describes a spiritual consequence of repeated refusal, which leaves them unable to see the meaning of the call.

phrases.translation: But the Messenger and the believers with him strived with their wealth and their lives. They will have all the best, and it is they who will be successful
phrases.explanation: The Messenger and believers with him strive with both resources and personal effort. The verse contrasts their active commitment with the hypocrites’ repeated requests to remain behind. The believers will receive what is good from Allah. The promise includes benefit and reward that outweigh the difficulty of their service. They are the successful because they respond faithfully and receive Allah’s reward. The verse measures success by commitment and lasting good, not by avoidance of hardship.

phrases.translation: Allah has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. That is the ultimate triumph
phrases.explanation: Allah prepares Gardens where believers will remain forever. The promise of permanence contrasts with the temporary comfort sought by those who refuse the call. The Gardens are called the ultimate triumph. The verse defines lasting success as reward from Allah in the Hereafter, not merely a comfortable worldly position.

phrases.translation: Some nomadic Arabs ˹also˺ came with excuses, seeking exemption.
phrases.explanation: Some nomadic Arabs arrive with excuses and ask to be exempt from the expedition. The verse recognizes that people approach the call differently and that reasons for staying behind must be assessed.

phrases.translation: And those who were untrue to Allah and His Messenger remained behind ˹with no excuse˺. The unfaithful among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Others who were untrue to Allah and the Messenger stay behind without a valid excuse. Their conduct distinguishes deliberate evasion from genuine inability. The unfaithful among them face painful punishment. The verse ties the warning to disloyalty and the lack of an honest reason, rather than treating every person unable to travel alike.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on the weak, the sick, or those lacking the means ˹if they stay behind˺, as long as they are true to Allah and His Messenger.
phrases.explanation: The weak, sick, and those without means are excused from staying behind if they remain sincere to Allah and the Messenger. The verse recognizes real limitations rather than demanding what people cannot do.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on the good-doers.
phrases.explanation: There is no blame on those who do good within their ability. The verse distinguishes sincere inability from deliberate refusal and avoids treating every person who stays behind as equally responsible.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful. These names reassure people with genuine limitations that Allah knows their circumstances and does not judge them as if they had refused out of hypocrisy.

phrases.translation: Nor ˹is there any blame on˺ those who came to you ˹O Prophet˺ for mounts,
phrases.explanation: Some believers come asking for transport so they can join the expedition. Their request shows a sincere desire to participate, even though they lack the means to make the journey.

phrases.translation: then when you said, “I can find no mounts for you,” they left with eyes overflowing with tears out of grief that they had nothing to contribute
phrases.explanation: They leave in tears when the Prophet cannot find mounts for them. Their grief reflects disappointment at being unable to contribute, rather than relief at avoiding danger. They grieve because they have nothing to offer. The verse recognizes the sincere people who wanted to serve but lacked resources, distinguishing them from those who had means and chose not to go.

phrases.translation: Blame is only on those who seek exemption from you although they have the means. They preferred to stay behind with the helpless,
phrases.explanation: Blame falls on those who ask to stay behind despite having the ability to join. The verse distinguishes deliberate avoidance from the genuine weakness or poverty mentioned just before. They prefer to remain with those who do not take part. The contrast shows that their choice is not forced by circumstances, but reflects a preference to avoid the call.

phrases.translation: and Allah has sealed their hearts so they do not realize ˹the consequences˺
phrases.explanation: Their hearts are sealed so they fail to realize the consequences. The verse portrays this as the result of persistent evasion and warns that repeated choices can dull moral understanding.

phrases.translation: They will make excuses to you ˹believers˺ when you return to them.
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites are expected to offer excuses when the believers return. The verse prepares the Prophet to recognize that these explanations may be attempts to manage appearances rather than honest accounts.

phrases.translation: Say, “Make no excuses, ˹for˺ we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us about your ˹true˺ state ˹of faith˺.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to accept their excuses because Allah has already disclosed their true state. The warning places private motives beyond the reach of their own attempts to conceal them.

phrases.translation: Your ˹future˺ deeds will be observed by Allah and His Messenger as well. And you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, then He will inform you of what you used to do.”
phrases.explanation: Their future deeds will be observed by Allah and the Messenger. This means their claims can be tested against later conduct rather than trusted without evidence. Everyone will return to the Knower of what is visible and hidden. The return to Allah makes accountability unavoidable, since both public actions and concealed motives are known. Allah will inform them of what they did. The verse closes by directing attention to final judgment, where excuses cannot replace an honest record of actions.

phrases.translation: When you return, they will swear to you by Allah so that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone—they are truly evil. Hell will be their home as a reward for what they have committed
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites swear to be left undisturbed. The instruction to leave them alone is followed by a judgment about their character, not an endorsement of their behavior. They are described as evil because of the conduct that the passage has exposed. Their oaths do not erase the lies or the deliberate refusal to support the community. Hell is named as the consequence of what they have committed. The verse connects their final outcome with their actions rather than treating punishment as unrelated to their choices.

phrases.translation: They will swear to you in order to please you. And even if you are pleased with them, Allah will never be pleased with the rebellious people
phrases.explanation: They swear repeatedly to regain the believers’ approval. The verse shows that pleasing people has become their goal, while sincere repentance and seeking Allah’s approval remain absent. Even if the believers are pleased, Allah will not be pleased with rebellious people. Human approval cannot replace a sincere relationship with Allah or make persistent rebellion acceptable.

phrases.translation: The nomadic Arabs ˹around Medina˺ are far worse in disbelief and hypocrisy,
phrases.explanation: The verse says many nomadic Arabs around Medina are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy. It describes a group in a particular setting, while the following verses also recognize believing nomads.

phrases.translation: and less likely to know the laws revealed by Allah to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Their distance from the community makes them less likely to know the laws revealed to the Messenger. The verse connects access to teaching with understanding, without implying that every nomad is the same. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. He knows the different conditions and intentions among people, and His judgment is not based on broad labels alone.

phrases.translation: And among the nomads are those who consider what they donate to be a loss and await your misfortune.
phrases.explanation: Some nomads regard charitable giving as a financial loss. The verse reveals a narrow view of provision that measures generosity only by what leaves one’s hands. They also wait for a misfortune to strike the believers. This expectation shows hostility toward the community and a lack of hope for its success.

phrases.translation: May ill-fortune befall them! And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: The verse answers their hostile wishes with a prayer that misfortune return upon them. Their ill will is exposed rather than rewarded. Allah hears and knows all things, including concealed hopes for others’ suffering. The attributes close the verse by affirming that such intentions are not hidden from Him.

phrases.translation: However, among the nomadic Arabs are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, and consider what they donate as a means of coming closer to Allah and ˹receiving˺ the prayers of the Messenger. It will certainly bring them closer. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Other nomads believe in Allah and the Last Day. Their faith gives meaning to their actions and contrasts with those who see charity as a loss. They give charity hoping to draw closer to Allah and receive the Messenger’s prayer. Their donation is an act of devotion and a request for spiritual benefit, not an obligation they resent. Their charity brings them closer to Allah, who admits them into His mercy. The verse presents giving as a path of devotion and hope for forgiveness.

phrases.translation: As for the foremost—the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers—and those who follow them in goodness, Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him.
phrases.explanation: The verse honors the earliest Emigrants and Helpers as well as those who follow them in goodness. It recognizes both foundational sacrifice and later faithful conduct. Allah is pleased with these believers, and they are pleased with Him. The relationship is mutual, joining divine approval with the believers’ contentment in their Lord.

phrases.translation: And He has prepared for them Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there for ever and ever. That is the ultimate triumph
phrases.explanation: Allah prepares Gardens with rivers where they will remain forever. The promise presents a lasting reward for those whose faithfulness and service shaped the early community. This eternal reward is the ultimate triumph. The verse defines success by Allah’s pleasure and lasting Paradise, not merely by worldly status or victory.

phrases.translation: Some of the nomads around you ˹believers˺ are hypocrites, as are some of the people of Medina. They have mastered hypocrisy.
phrases.explanation: Hypocrites are found among both nearby nomads and people of Medina. The verse cautions the community not to assume that hypocrisy belongs only to outsiders. Some have become practiced in concealing their intentions. Their skill at appearing loyal makes discernment difficult for other people.

phrases.translation: They are not known to you ˹O Prophet˺; they are known to Us. We will punish them twice ˹in this world˺, then they will be brought back ˹to their Lord˺ for a tremendous punishment
phrases.explanation: The Prophet may not know all of them, but Allah knows them fully. Hidden hypocrisy is not hidden from Allah, who sees what people cannot. They will face punishment in this world and then a tremendous punishment when returned to their Lord. The verse warns that concealment does not cancel accountability.

phrases.translation: Some others have confessed their wrongdoing: they have mixed goodness with evil. It is right to hope that Allah will turn to them in mercy. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Some people openly confess that they have done wrong. Their admission is a first step toward repentance, unlike the excuses and denials described in the preceding verses. Their lives have included both good and evil deeds. The verse does not treat them as beyond hope, but acknowledges the mixed record they must bring honestly before Allah. It is right to hope that Allah will accept their repentance. His forgiveness and mercy remain available to people who acknowledge wrongdoing and sincerely turn back.

phrases.translation: Take from their wealth ˹O Prophet˺ charity to purify and bless them, and pray for them—surely your prayer is a source of comfort for them. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to take charity from their wealth to purify and bless them. Giving corrects attachment to wealth and becomes a means of spiritual growth. He is also told to pray for them. His prayer comforts the donors and shows that charity is part of a relationship of care between the community and its leadership. Allah hears and knows all things. He hears the prayer and knows the sincerity behind the donation, so neither giving nor supplication is overlooked.

phrases.translation: Do they not know that Allah alone accepts the repentance of His servants and receives ˹their˺ charity, and that Allah alone is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah alone accepts repentance and receives charity. The verse emphasizes that these acts are directed to Him, even when the Prophet administers the community’s giving. Allah is the Accepter of Repentance and Most Merciful. These names encourage people to return to Him and give sincerely, confident that their efforts are met with mercy.

phrases.translation: Tell ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Do as you will. Your deeds will be observed by Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to address those whose sincerity is in question. The phrase challenges them to act, knowing that their choices will reveal their intentions. Allah, the Messenger, and the believers will observe their deeds. Their conduct over time will show whether their claims are sincere, and will be part of their accountability.

phrases.translation: And you will be returned to the Knower of the seen and unseen, then He will inform you of what you used to do.”
phrases.explanation: They will return to the Knower of the visible and hidden. No action or motive is outside Allah’s knowledge, so the apparent success of deception is temporary. Allah will inform them of what they used to do. The warning makes clear that every deed will be disclosed and judged, even if people kept it concealed in life.

phrases.translation: And some others are left for Allah’s decision, either to punish them
phrases.explanation: Some people are left for Allah’s decision, rather than being immediately classified with those whose conduct is already clear. The verse leaves open either punishment or mercy according to His knowledge and wisdom.

phrases.translation: or turn to them in mercy. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. He knows what each person has done and determines the outcome with wisdom, even when the community does not yet know how to judge them.

phrases.translation: There are also those ˹hypocrites˺ who set up a mosque ˹only˺ to cause harm,
phrases.explanation: The verse describes a mosque established by hypocrites with the intention of causing harm. It criticizes this specific building and its purpose, not mosques generally or everyone who attends one.

phrases.translation: promote disbelief, divide the believers, and as a base for those who had previously fought against Allah and His Messenger.
phrases.explanation: The building is also meant to promote disbelief, divide the believers, and shelter those who had fought Allah and His Messenger. The list explains why its appearance as a mosque cannot make its purpose sincere.

phrases.translation: They will definitely swear, “We intended nothing but good,” but Allah bears witness that they are surely liars
phrases.explanation: Its builders swear that they intended only good, but the verse identifies their claim as false. Their stated purpose conflicts with the harm and division the building was designed to cause. Allah bears witness that they are liars. The warning reminds readers that religious language and appearances cannot conceal a purpose known to Allah.

phrases.translation: Do not ˹O Prophet˺ ever pray in it.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to pray in the building described as established for harm and division. The instruction concerns this particular place and its intention, not a general ban on prayer in mosques.

phrases.translation: Certainly, a mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy of your prayers.
phrases.explanation: A mosque founded on righteousness from its first day is more worthy of prayer. The verse makes the purpose and foundation of a place important, not merely its name or outward form.

phrases.translation: In it are men who love to be purified. And Allah loves those who purify themselves
phrases.explanation: The people associated with the righteous mosque love purification. Their care for purity is presented as a sign of sincere worship and a desire to approach Allah in a fitting way. Allah loves those who purify themselves. The verse connects physical and spiritual readiness for worship with a quality beloved to Allah.

phrases.translation: Which is better: those who laid the foundation of their building on the fear and pleasure of Allah, or those who did so on the edge of a crumbling cliff that tumbled down with them into the Fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people
phrases.explanation: One foundation is built on reverence for Allah and hope for His pleasure. The image presents faith and sincere intention as a stable base for a person’s actions. The opposing foundation rests on a crumbling cliff that collapses with its builder into Hell. The image contrasts a secure moral basis with a choice that cannot bear weight or last. Allah does not guide wrongdoing people. The conclusion connects the collapse to wrongdoing and warns that an apparently impressive structure cannot rescue a corrupt foundation.

phrases.translation: The building which they erected will never cease to fuel hypocrisy in their hearts until their hearts are torn apart. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: The mosque built for harm continues to feed hypocrisy in its builders’ hearts until their hearts are torn apart. The verse portrays the lasting inner damage caused by a project founded on deceit. Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise. He knows the hidden purpose behind the building and the consequences that follow, even if people initially mistake its outward appearance for good.

phrases.translation: Allah has indeed purchased from the believers their lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise.
phrases.explanation: The verse describes Allah’s promise to believers as an exchange of their lives and wealth for Paradise. It presents their sacrifice as part of a covenant with Allah, not a claim that human life has no value.

phrases.translation: They fight in the cause of Allah and kill or are killed.
phrases.explanation: The verse speaks of fighting in the cause of Allah and the possibility of death in battle. In the surah’s setting, this concerns organized conflict and sacrifice, not private violence or self-harm.

phrases.translation: This is a true promise binding on Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran.
phrases.explanation: The promise is said to be binding in the Torah, Gospel, and Quran. The verse connects the commitment to a continuing history of revelation and assures believers that Allah’s promise is dependable.

phrases.translation: And whose promise is truer than Allah’s? So rejoice in the exchange you have made with Him. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question asks whether anyone’s promise could be truer than Allah’s. The verse invites confidence in His word rather than doubt about the reward promised. Believers are told to rejoice in the exchange they have made with Allah. Their joy comes from trusting His promise, not from taking pride in worldly power. This is described as the ultimate triumph. The verse defines success through Allah’s promised reward and approval, beyond any temporary outcome in battle.

phrases.translation: ˹It is the believers˺ who repent, who are devoted to worship, who praise ˹their Lord˺, who fast, who bow down and prostrate themselves,
phrases.explanation: Believers repent, worship, and praise Allah. These qualities show a relationship marked by returning to Him, serving Him, and remembering His goodness. They fast, bow, and prostrate in worship. The verse portrays devotion through several practices that discipline the body and direct the heart toward Allah.

phrases.translation: who encourage good and forbid evil, and who observe the limits set by Allah. And give good news to the believers
phrases.explanation: Believers encourage good and forbid evil, taking responsibility for the moral health of the community rather than limiting faith to private worship. They also observe the limits Allah has set. Respecting boundaries completes the picture of devotion by joining worship with careful conduct. The Prophet is told to give good news to these believers. Their repentance, worship, moral care, and observance of limits are grounds for hope in Allah’s reward.

phrases.translation: It is not ˹proper˺ for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives,
phrases.explanation: The verse addresses seeking forgiveness for polytheists, even when they are close relatives, after their final rejection has become clear. It speaks to this specific circumstance, not to mistreating living relatives or blocking them from guidance.

phrases.translation: after it has become clear to the believers that they are bound for the Hellfire
phrases.explanation: Once the believers know that a person has died rejecting faith, the Prophet and believers are told not to seek forgiveness for them. The verse sets a boundary after death and final rejection.

phrases.translation: As for Abraham’s prayer for his father’s forgiveness, it was only in fulfilment of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to Abraham that his father was an enemy of Allah, he broke ties with him. Abraham was truly tender-hearted, forbearing
phrases.explanation: Abraham’s prayer for his father fulfilled a promise he had made. The verse explains the prayer in the context of that promise, not as approval of his father’s beliefs. When Abraham realized his father was an enemy of Allah, he ended that bond. The verse shows that family attachment does not override a clear rejection of Allah. Abraham is described as tender-hearted and forbearing. His compassion explains his earlier prayer, while his patience and clarity shape the decision that followed.

phrases.translation: Allah would never consider a people deviant after He has guided them, until He makes clear to them what they must avoid. Surely Allah has ˹full˺ knowledge of everything
phrases.explanation: Allah does not hold a people blameworthy for failing to avoid something until He has made it clear. The verse links accountability with guidance and fair notice. Allah knows everything fully. His knowledge encompasses what people understood and what they did, grounding judgment in complete awareness of their circumstances.

phrases.translation: Indeed, to Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And besides Allah you have no guardian or helper
phrases.explanation: The heavens and earth belong to Allah, who gives life and causes death. The verse emphasizes His authority over existence and the limits of every human power. No guardian or helper exists besides Allah in the ultimate sense. The reminder turns believers toward Him for protection and aid rather than relying on created beings as independent powers.

phrases.translation: Allah has certainly turned in mercy to the Prophet as well as the Emigrants and the Helpers who stood by him in the time of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had almost faltered. He then accepted their repentance. Surely He is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to them
phrases.explanation: Allah turned in mercy to the Prophet, Emigrants, and Helpers who stood by him during hardship. The verse recalls their loyalty when the community faced a difficult expedition. Some hearts nearly wavered under the strain, yet Allah accepted their repentance. The verse recognizes human weakness while emphasizing that people can return to faith after faltering. Allah is Ever-Gracious and Most Merciful to them. The closing highlights the mercy that restored the believers and accompanied them through a demanding moment.

phrases.translation: And ˹Allah has also turned in mercy to˺ the three who had remained behind, ˹whose guilt distressed them˺ until the earth, despite its vastness, seemed to close in on them, and their souls were torn in anguish.
phrases.explanation: The three who stayed behind felt the earth close in and their souls grieve. The image conveys the weight of waiting for judgment after their failure to join the expedition.

phrases.translation: They knew there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Surely Allah ˹alone˺ is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: They understood that there was no refuge from Allah except through turning back to Him. Their distress leads them away from excuses and toward honest dependence. Allah turns to them in mercy so they may repent. The verse presents divine mercy as a path back to faithfulness, not as a denial that their earlier choice was wrong. Allah alone accepts repentance and is Most Merciful. The conclusion offers hope to people who acknowledge their failure and return sincerely.

phrases.translation: O believers! Be mindful of Allah and be with the truthful
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to remain mindful of Allah, keeping His guidance and accountability in view. This orientation shapes decisions in both public and private life. They are also told to stay with the truthful. The verse encourages companionship with people whose honesty supports faithful conduct and helps the community resist hypocrisy.

phrases.translation: It was not ˹proper˺ for the people of Medina and the nomadic Arabs around them to avoid marching with the Messenger of Allah or to prefer their own lives above his.
phrases.explanation: The people of Medina and surrounding nomads should not avoid marching with the Messenger or put their own lives above his. The verse describes a serious communal duty in the campaign.

phrases.translation: That is because whenever they suffer from thirst, fatigue, or hunger in the cause of Allah; or tread on a territory, unnerving the disbelievers;
phrases.explanation: Thirst, fatigue, and hunger endured in Allah’s cause are counted as good deeds. The verse recognizes the real hardships of service rather than treating them as wasted effort. Even crossing territory in a way that unsettles the opposing force is recorded as good. The setting is an organized campaign, where movement itself can affect the conflict.

phrases.translation: or inflict any loss on an enemy—
phrases.explanation: Any loss inflicted on an enemy in the campaign is counted to the believers’ credit. The phrase describes the conflict already under way, not a general instruction to harm people outside it.

phrases.translation: it is written to their credit as a good deed. Surely Allah never discounts the reward of the good-doers
phrases.explanation: These efforts are recorded as good deeds. The verse reassures the believers that hardship, travel, and service all count when undertaken sincerely in Allah’s cause. Allah never discounts the reward of those who do good. The closing promises that no sincere effort in the campaign is overlooked, even if it seems small.

phrases.translation: And whenever they make a donation, small or large, or cross a valley ˹in Allah’s cause˺—
phrases.explanation: Every donation counts, whether small or large. The verse values sincere generosity rather than measuring a person’s devotion only by the size of a gift. Crossing a valley in Allah’s cause is also recorded. The journey and effort of service matter alongside the financial donation.

phrases.translation: it is written to their credit, so that Allah may grant them the best reward for what they used to do
phrases.explanation: These acts are written to the believers’ credit. The image assures them that no contribution or effort disappears unnoticed. Allah will grant them the best reward for what they did. The verse ends by placing hope in divine recompense, which exceeds the immediate value of their actions.

phrases.translation: ˹However,˺ it is not necessary for the believers to march forth all at once. Only a party from each group should march forth, leaving the rest to gain religious knowledge
phrases.explanation: The believers are not required to march forth all together. The verse allows the community to meet its responsibilities through an organized distribution of roles. A party from each group should go forth while others remain to gain religious knowledge. The instruction recognizes that learning is itself an essential service to the community.

phrases.translation: then enlighten their people when they return to them, so that they ˹too˺ may beware ˹of evil˺
phrases.explanation: Those who learn should teach their people after returning. Knowledge is meant to be shared, so the wider community can understand and practice its faith. Teaching helps people beware of evil. The verse balances urgent public duties with education, ensuring that believers are informed rather than left without guidance.

phrases.translation: O believers! Fight the disbelievers around you
phrases.explanation: The believers are told to confront disbelieving enemies around them in the conflict addressed by the surah. The command is situated in an organized campaign, not a license for indiscriminate violence.

phrases.translation: and let them find firmness in you. And know that Allah is with those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: The opposing force should encounter resolve from the believers. The instruction calls for courage and steadiness in a defined conflict, not cruelty or excess. Allah is with those mindful of Him. The verse links steadfastness with moral restraint and awareness of Allah, reminding believers that conduct matters even in conflict.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, some of them ask ˹mockingly˺, “Which of you has this increased in faith?” As for the believers, it has increased them in faith and they rejoice
phrases.explanation: Some people mockingly ask whether a newly revealed surah has increased anyone’s faith. Their question treats revelation with contempt rather than considering its guidance seriously. For believers, revelation increases faith and brings joy. The same message can expose different responses: sincere people welcome guidance, while those who mock it reveal their own attitude.

phrases.translation: But as for those with sickness in their hearts, it has increased them only in wickedness upon their wickedness, and they die as disbelievers
phrases.explanation: For people with sickness in their hearts, revelation adds to their wickedness. The verse describes how they respond to guidance with further resistance rather than humility. They die as disbelievers. The warning concerns the persistent state of those described, not people who struggle, repent, or seek greater understanding.

phrases.translation: Do they not see that they are tried once or twice every year? Yet they neither repent nor do they learn a lesson
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether these people notice that they face trials repeatedly, once or twice each year. Recurring difficulty can prompt reflection and expose the fragility of their claims. Despite these reminders, they neither repent nor learn a lesson. The criticism is not that trials automatically make faith easy, but that they refuse to reflect or change.

phrases.translation: Whenever a sûrah is revealed, they look at one another, ˹saying,˺ “Is anyone watching you?” Then they slip away. ˹It is˺ Allah ˹Who˺ has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not comprehend
phrases.explanation: When a surah is revealed, they exchange glances and ask whether anyone is watching. Their reaction suggests discomfort with being seen in their contempt for revelation. They leave rather than listen openly. Their quiet withdrawal reinforces the pattern of evasion described throughout the passage. Allah turns their hearts away because they do not comprehend. The verse connects this outcome with their persistent refusal to engage sincerely with guidance.

phrases.translation: There certainly has come to you a messenger from among yourselves. He is concerned by your suffering, anxious for your well-being, and gracious and merciful to the believers
phrases.explanation: The messenger comes from among the people he addresses. This closeness makes his concern understandable and his guidance accessible to the community. He is pained by their suffering and deeply concerned for their welfare. The verse presents the Prophet’s leadership as compassionate rather than indifferent to people’s hardships. He is gracious and merciful to the believers. These qualities describe the care with which he guides them and the kindness that should mark their relationship with him.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, then say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah is sufficient for me.
phrases.explanation: If people turn away, the Prophet is told to affirm that Allah is sufficient for him. The statement expresses trust in Allah without making the success of the message depend on everyone’s acceptance.

phrases.translation: There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. In Him I put my trust. And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.”
phrases.explanation: Allah alone deserves worship, and the Prophet places his trust in Him. This belief grounds reliance in Allah rather than in human approval or power. Allah is Lord of the Mighty Throne. The closing title emphasizes His supreme authority and gives the Prophet a firm basis for trust when facing rejection.
